author: Ljungh, 1813
summary: 해마다 10건 미만으로 드물게 기록되는 새로, 우리나라 중부 이북과 서북 해안 지대에서 산다. 둥지는 땅 위에 잘 숨겨 짓고 한배에 알을 7~9개 낳으며, 암컷은 2년째 여름부터 번식한다. 동북아시아에 분포하고 동남아시아에서 겨울을 난다.

art.subject: Band-bellied Crake (Zapornia paykullii), adult in summer: crown, nape, back, wings and tail dark olive-brown and unmarked, except thin white bars across the wing coverts; face, sides of the neck and breast warm chestnut, slightly paler towards the centre of the breast; throat almost white; flanks, belly and undertail coverts boldly barred black and white; short stout bill, pale greenish-grey with a darker culmen and a dark tip; red eye; legs and feet salmon-red to orange-red.
art.pose: standing on the ground among dense vegetation, side view
art.scene: Korean summer coastal lowland in the northwest with dense grassy cover; no people, buildings or text
views: adult, side view standing in grass: dark olive-brown upperparts with thin white bars on the wing coverts, almost white throat, chestnut face and breast, black-and-white barred flanks and belly, salmon-red legs with long toes
adult, head detail in profile: dark olive-brown crown, chestnut face, almost white throat, red eye, short stout pale greenish-grey bill with a darker culmen and a dark tip
art.build: Small crake, about 20cm, roughly thrush-sized and a little larger and stouter than Ruddy-breasted Crake; body strongly compressed side to side for slipping through dense vegetation, with a short tail. No crest; the crown feathers lie flat. Bill short and stout, much shorter than the head. Legs fairly long, salmon-red, with long toes. Wings short and rounded; at rest the wingtips reach the base of the tail. Walks with a horizontal body; flies low and weakly with the legs dangling.
avoid: Do not paint plain wing coverts and a dark, faintly barred belly; that is Ruddy-breasted Crake (Zapornia fusca).
Do not paint a long bill (Water Rail), or a grey face and breast with a white-streaked back (Baillon's Crake).
Do not paint the legs green or yellow; they are salmon-red.
Do not paint the belly plain; the flanks and belly are boldly barred black and white.
